steps.text: Read the Terms of Service, and scroll all the way to the bottom.
Then tap Disclaimer, and scroll that to the bottom too.
Tap I Accept — Continue.
After you accept, follow the next few screens until you reach Home. Then bring in a bank statement so Home fills in with your own numbers.
To change the language, tap the menu.
Tap Preferences.
Tap Language.
Pick a language from the list. Each one is shown in its own words, like Español for Spanish.
The whole app switches right away. To switch back, tap Language again and pick English.
Back in English.
On Home, tap Import your bank statement.
Tap Try sample statement.
The charges are listed. Leave them checked.
Tap Import 10 new transactions.
The summary shows income, expenses, and what is left.
Back on Home, your numbers are filled in.
Home shows the month at a glance: what came in, what went out, and the difference.
Below that, setup continues with your income and a bill.
Tap Activity to see every transaction.
Activity lists every transaction for the month.
Tap Activity to see every transaction. The top shows what you spent, what came in, and the difference for the month.
Use the arrows to move between months.
Tap Expenses to see only money going out.
Tap Income for money coming in.
Tap All to see everything again.
Tap a transaction to open it.
Here you see the amount, the date, and the line from your statement.
Tap back to return to the list.
To add a transaction yourself, tap the round button with the pencil on it.
Tap 10 dollars.
Tap Save.
It is in your list right away.
Tap Budget. The top compares what you spent this month with what came in.
Below that is your spending in each category.
Tap Goals, then Start a savings goal.
Name the goal, and type the target amount.
Type a target date.
Tap Add Goal.
The card shows the goal, the date, and what to set aside each month.
Tap Add funds.
Tap 100 dollars, then Add Funds.
The progress moves right away.
Tap Budget, then Bills.
Tap Add a Bill.
Name the bill, and type the amount. The due day is the day of the month.
Choose 3 days before.
Tap Add Bill.
The bill shows the due day, the days left, and the reminder.
When you've paid it, tap Mark Paid.
It leaves the list of what's due.
Tap Goals, then Track a debt.
No account numbers are stored. Type a name you'll recognize.
Type the balance, the rate, and the minimum payment.
Tap Add Debt.
One account, an $85 minimum, 6.9 percent, and debt-free in 2 years 7 months.
Tap Compare Strategies.
Avalanche pays the highest interest first. Snowball pays the lowest balance first.
With one debt, both show 2 years 7 months and 226 dollars in interest.
Tap Coach, then Reports.
Open Tax & business, then Mileage Log.
Tap the round button.
Business is the trip type. Type the miles. 18 miles at 70 cents comes to 12 dollars and 60 cents.
Type what the trip was for. This one is a client meeting.
Tap Save. The year shows 18 miles, one trip, and 13 dollars deductible.
Your net worth is what you own minus what you owe. Tap Coach, then Reports.
Open Quarterly planning, then Net Worth History.
Nothing to chart yet. Tap Go to My Assets.
To add something you own, tap the round button.
Type a name and what it is worth, and pick a category. This one is a retirement account, 18 thousand dollars, under Investment.
Tap Add Asset.
Net worth is 18 thousand dollars. Debts are zero.
Have a question about your money? Tap Coach, then Ask.
Tap a suggested question. This one asks how you are doing this month.
20 dollars went out, and nothing came in, so the savings rate is zero. Tap Cash flow.
October shows 20 dollars spent.
Tap Search, then type backup.
Tap Backup and Restore.
Tap Create Full Backup.
Saved on this phone. Tap Done. Share to PC or email is there when you want a copy somewhere else.
On a new phone, come back here and tap Restore from Backup.
